meta.excerpt: Dachshund grooming depends entirely on coat type: smooth coats need almost nothing, wirehaired coats need hand-stripping, and longhaired coats need regular brushing. Here's what each requires.
meta.meta_description: Dachshund grooming guide for all three coat types — smooth, long-haired, and wirehaired — with brushing schedule, hand-stripping vs trimming, and tools.

intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: Dachshund Grooming: It Depends on Your Coat Type
intro.html:
Dachshunds come in three coat types — smooth, wirehaired, and longhaired — and the grooming requirements vary significantly between them. Before you start any routine, identify which coat type you have.

  • Smooth coat: Almost no grooming required. The lowest-maintenance option.
  • Wirehaired coat: Requires hand-stripping (or clipping) 1–2 times per year plus regular beard and brow tidying. Moderate maintenance.
  • Longhaired coat: Regular brushing to prevent tangles, especially behind the ears and on the chest feathering. Moderate maintenance.

All three coat types share the same nail and dental care needs — and nails in particular matter for Dachshunds, since long nails alter gait and put extra stress on a spine that's already at high IVDD risk.

care.label: Coat-by-Coat Routine
care.heading: Grooming by Coat Type
care.html:
Smooth Coat

The smoothhaired Dachshund is arguably the easiest dog to groom. A quick wipe with a damp cloth or chamois keeps the coat gleaming. Bathe every 6–8 weeks. Brush weekly with a soft bristle brush or grooming mitt to remove loose hair. Professional grooming: optional nail trim only.

Wirehaired Coat

The wiry outercoat should ideally be maintained through hand-stripping — pulling the dead outer coat by hand rather than cutting it. This preserves coat texture and color. Clipping (using scissors/clippers) is faster but softens the coat over time. Most pet owners use a groomer for this 1–2 times per year. In between, trim the beard and eyebrows monthly to keep them tidy and prevent food from collecting in the beard.

Longhaired Coat

Brush 2–3 times per week with a slicker brush and steel comb. Focus on the feathering behind the ears, chest, belly, and tail — these areas mat first. A detangling spray helps on knot-prone days. Professional grooming every 8–12 weeks for a tidy trim of the feathering keeps maintenance manageable at home.

All Coat Types: Nails & Teeth

Nails: Trim every 3–4 weeks. This is non-optional for Dachshunds — long nails change the way the foot strikes the ground, altering posture and adding load to an already-vulnerable spine. If you hear clicking on hard floors, they're overdue.

Teeth: Brush 3–4 times per week. Small breeds are prone to dental disease, and Dachshunds are no exception.

special.label: Grooming & Spine Safety
special.heading: Grooming Positions and IVDD Risk
special.html:
Because Dachshunds are at significant risk for intervertebral disc disease (IVDD), grooming position matters. A startled or uncomfortable dog on a grooming table may jump — and a fall from even table height can cause spinal injury.

Safe Grooming Practices

  • Always groom on a non-slip surface or have one hand supporting the dog
  • For nail trims, consider grooming on the floor rather than a raised table
  • Avoid positioning the dog in ways that arch or twist the spine
  • If your dog is tense or resistant, go slowly — a stressed dog is more likely to lunge
  • Professional groomers should be told your dog has IVDD risk and to keep them secured

Introduce grooming early and pair it with treats so it becomes a calm, cooperative experience. A Dachshund that tolerates handling confidently is safer in any grooming scenario.

faq.q: What's the difference between hand-stripping and clipping for wirehaired Dachshunds?
faq.a: Hand-stripping removes the dead outer coat by pulling it out at the root — this preserves the wiry texture and correct color of the coat. Clipping cuts the hair, which over time softens the texture and fades the color. For show dogs, hand-stripping is required. For pets, clipping is perfectly acceptable and most groomers offer it.

faq.q: How often should I trim my Dachshund's nails?
faq.a: Every 3–4 weeks. Long nails are especially problematic for Dachshunds because they alter gait and add stress to the spine. If you hear clicking on hard floors, trim immediately.

faq.q: My longhaired Dachshund's coat is getting matted — what should I do?
faq.a: Apply a detangling spray and work through mats with your fingers before reaching for a comb. Always hold the mat at the base to avoid pulling the skin. Prevention is far easier — brush 2–3 times per week and pay attention to ears, chest, and belly feathering.

Smooth coats rarely do. Wirehaired coats benefit from professional hand-stripping or clipping 1–2 times per year. Longhaired coats benefit from professional trims every 8–12 weeks. All three types can go to a groomer for nail trims if needed.
